column2: From him Parameshthi; from him Pratihara, his lineage; from Pratihara Pratiharta; from Pratiharta, Bhuva;
then Udgitha and Prastara; from Prastara the son Vibhu; then Prithu; then Nakta; and Nakta's son was Gaya;
Nara was Gaya's son; his son was Viraj; his son was the mighty Dhiman, born from him;
Mahanta was his son; Manasya his offspring; Tvashta; from Tvashta, Viraja; Rajas was his son too;
of Rajas, Satyajit, O sage, a hundred sons were born; with Vishvajyoti chief, by them Bharata was increased;
by the creation of the Krita, Treta and other ages, the Svayambhuva creation is remembered.
The Sea, the Chakshus, the Saumya Sea, Bhadra, Uttara Kurus; Aneela, Nishadha-ayama, Malyavan and Gandhamadana;
between them stands Meru in the form of a pericarp; Bharatas, Ketumalas, Bhadrashvas and Kurus likewise
are the petals of the world-lotus outside the boundary mountains. Jathara and Devakuta are the two boundary mountains,
extending south and north, reaching Nila and Nishadha; Gandhamadana and Kailasa as before both extending;
eighty yojanas in length, placed within the ocean; Nishadha and Pariyatra are the two boundary mountains,
in the western part of Meru, as in the east they stand. Trishringa and Rudhira are the northern year-mountains,
as before five-part, set within the ocean. Jathara and others are the boundary mountains in the four directions of Meru.
In the valleys at Keshara and others there are cities of Lakshmi, Vishnu, Agni, Sun and other gods, O best of sages,
of earthly beings and heaven-natured ones; sinners do not go there. In Bhadrashva is Hayagriva; in Ketumala, Varaha;
in Bharata, Kurma-formed; in the Kurus, Matsya-formed; the Lord Hari is worshipped everywhere in universal form.
In the eight lands beginning with Kimpurusha there is no hunger, fear, sorrow and the like; the people live twenty-four thousand years without disease.
There is no imagining of Krita and other ages; there are earthly waters and no clouds. In all these years there are seven and seven family mountains,
and hundreds of rivers, born from them, as sacred places. The sacred places that are in Bharata, those I tell you.
Vinashana is a meritorious sacred place; Nagodbheda destroying sin; Kumarakoti, and always named;
I shall go to Kurukshetra; I live in Kurukshetra — who always says thus becomes pure and attains heaven.
There Vishnu and other gods; by living there one goes to Hari. One who bathes at Sarasvati at Sannihiti shares Brahma's world.
Even the dust of Kurukshetra leads to the highest goal. Dharmatirtha, Suvarna, Gangadvara the unsurpassed,
Kanakhala the meritorious sacred place, and Bhadrakarna pool; the confluence of Ganga and Sarasvati, Brahmavarta, destroying sin;
Bhrigutunga, Kubjamra, Gangodbheda ending sin; Varanasi the best sacred place, Avimukta unsurpassed;
Kapalamochana, Prayaga the king of sacred places; the confluence of Gomati and Ganga; Ganga everywhere gives heaven;
Rajagriha the meritorious sacred place, Shalagrama ending sin; Vatesha, Vamana-tirtha, Kalika-sangama the best;
Lauhitya, Karatoya, Shona, and the supreme Arshabha; Shriparvata, Kolvagiri, Sahyadri, Malaya mountain;
Godavari, Tungabhadra, Kaveri, the boon-giving river; Tapi, Payoshni, Reva, and the excellent Dandakaranya;
Kalanjara, Munjavata sacred place, the supreme Shurparaka; Mandakini, Chitrakuta, the supreme Shringaverapura;
Avanti the supreme sacred place; Ayodhya the destroyer of sin; Naimisha the supreme sacred place giving enjoyment and liberation.
There at Prayaga the Vedas and sacrifices are embodied. By praising this sacred place, even by chanting its name,
or by taking its clay, one is freed from all sins. At Prayaga gifts at the confluence, ancestral rites and recitation and the like are imperishable.
Not by the word of gods, O Brahmin, nor by the word of people — one's mind turns to death at Prayaga at the end.
Ten thousand sacred places and sixty crores more — their presence is here alone; Prayaga is supreme at the end.
Here is Bhogavati of Vasuki; Hamsaprapatana is supreme; the fruit of giving a crore of cows is the fruit of bathing there for three days
at Prayaga in the month of Magha — so say the wise. Ganga is easily had everywhere, hard to get in three places:
Gangadvara, Prayaga and Gangasagara-sangama. By giving here one goes to heaven and is born here a king of kings.
One who dies at the root of the banyan, at the confluence and elsewhere goes to Vishnu's city. The lovely Urvashi's sandbank, the sacred place of Sandhyavata,
Kotitirtha, Ashvamedha, the best Ganga-Yamuna; Manasa free of dust; Vasaraka the supreme sacred place.
Kedara is supreme and secret; eight are in Avimukta. Of secrets the supreme secret is Avimukta, my supreme.
It was two yojanas in the east, half a yojana otherwise. There was the river Varana; between the two is Varanasi.
Here bathing, repetition, oblation, death, worship of gods, ancestral rites, giving and residence — whatever it be, gives enjoyment and liberation.
All around the mountain they stay at Amarakantaka. The meritorious confluence with the Kaveri; now hear of Shriparvata.
Gauri, in the form of Shri, performed austerity; Hari said to her: "You will attain the spiritual; Shriparvata will be your name.
Around it a hundred yojanas will be greatly meritorious. Here gift, austerity, recitation, ancestral rites — all are imperishable;
death here leads to Shiva's world; the best sacred place giving all." Hara sports here with the Goddess, and Hiranyakashipu likewise,
having performed austerity became mighty; the sages attained accomplishment.
Again Brahma said to Vishnu: at the full time the demon moved. Vishnu then called Dharma and spoke of a divine-made stone:
All gods, hold it; let them be above it. The Gadadhara, my form, will stay with the gods.
Dharma, hearing that, bore the supreme divine stone. The daughter born of Dharma and Dharmavati, Dharmavrata,
Marichi, Brahma's son, wed her, endowed with austerity. As Hari sported with Shri, so Shambhu with Gauri — so he with her.
Having brought kusha, flowers and the rest from the forest, very tired, having eaten, he said to Dharmavrata: "Massage my feet."
Saying "So be it," the beloved massaged the sage's feet as he rested. In the meantime, when the sage slept, Brahma came.
Dharmavrata thought: "Whom shall I honor — Brahma? Or massage the feet? Brahma is worthy, teacher of teachers."
Having reflected, she honored Brahma with offerings and the rest. Marichi saw her and, for transgression of his word, cursed her:
You shall become a stone, from anger. Dharmavrata said to him: "Leaving the massage, I honored your teacher;
I am blameless; since you will get a curse from Shankara." Dharmavrata, bearing the curse separately, went into the fire,
and performed austerity for ten thousand thousands of years. Then Vishnu and the other gods said: "Ask a boon."
Dharmavrata said to the gods: "Let my curse be reversed." The gods said: "The curse given by Marichi will be, not otherwise.
You will be a stone, pure, marked by the gods' feet; Devavrata, Devashila, of the form of all the gods and the rest,
made of all gods, meritorious, immovable." Devavrata said: "If you are pleased with me, may all stay in me always:
Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra and the rest, the gods led by Gauri and Lakshmi." Agni said: Hearing Devavrata's words, saying "So be it," they went to heaven.
That divine stone was held by Dharma on this demon. With the stone the demon moved; then Rudra and the others stood on it.
With the gods the demon moved; then he was appeased by the gods; Hari, going to the milk-ocean, gave his own form, Shri-Gadadhara.
Go; I shall go myself with a form reachable by the gods. The god Gadadhara stood, of both manifest and unmanifest nature.
For immovability, the god himself stood as Adi-Gadadhara. A demon named Gada, a Daitya, was slain by Vishnu long ago;
the first mace made of his bones by Vishvakarman — with the first mace Heti and the chief Rakshasas were slain
by Gadadhara duly; therefore Adi-Gadadhara. When the primal Gadadhara stood on the divine stone,
Gayasura became immovable; Brahma gave the full oblation. Gayasura said to the gods: "Why was I cheated?
By mere word of Vishnu I would be immovable; if I am overcome, gods, you should grant me a boon."
The gods said: "Since we made you immovable for making a sacred place, a field of Vishnu, Shambhu and Brahma will be yours,
famous above all sacred places, giving ancestors Brahma's world." Saying so, the gods stood, and goddesses, sacred places and the rest.
Having performed the sacrifice, Brahma then gave fees to the priests: the Gaya field of five krosha and fifty-five villages he gave,
making golden mountains, rivers flowing with milk and honey, lakes of curds and ghee, many mountains of food and the like,
a wish-fulfilling cow, wish-fulfilling tree, houses of gold and silver. The lord gave, telling the best Brahmins not to ask for little.
At the dharma sacrifice, from greed, having accepted wealth and the rest, when they stayed at the end of Gaya they were cursed by Brahma:
You will be without learning, full of craving; rivers without milk and the like, mountains in stone form.
The Brahmins said to Brahma: "Everything is destroyed by the curse; grant us grace for livelihood, make us Brahmins." He said:

You will be livelihood-dependent on the sacred place as long as moon and sun; the men who come to Gaya and worship you
agnipuran:114:40	with offerings to gods and ancestors, with wealth and faith — a hundred of their families go from hell to heaven, from heaven to the supreme goal.
Gaya too performed a sacrifice, with much food and many fees; Gayapuri by that name; the Pandavas worshipped Hari.

I have come to this Gaya as the giver of pinda for them. In the north of Mundaprishtha, worshipped by hosts of divine sages,
agnipuran:115:23	the sacred place named Kanakhala, famed in the three worlds, with those that give pleasure to the perfected and terrify sinners,
agnipuran:115:24	with licking great serpents is always guarded. Bathing there, men go to heaven and sport on earth.
